subject: Chemistry
learning_objectives: Identify the products at the cathode and anode.
definition: Electrolysis is the chemical decomposition of an electrolyte by the passage of electric current.
simple_explanation: When electricity passes through a molten or aqueous ionic substance, positive ions move to the cathode while negative ions move to the anode where chemical reactions occur.
detailed_explanation: Electrolysis uses electrical energy to drive a non-spontaneous chemical reaction. Positive ions gain electrons at the cathode (reduction), while negative ions lose electrons at the anode (oxidation).
common_mistakes: Confusing the cathode with the anode.
Forgetting that reduction occurs at the cathode.
Ignoring the effect of inert and active electrodes.
exam_tips: Determine whether the solution is molten or aqueous.
practice_questions: Write the cathode equation for copper(II) sulphate solution using inert electrodes.
answers: Electrolysis is the chemical decomposition of an electrolyte by the passage of electric current.
